items.title: Synthetic NTFS crash fixtures with auxiliary ntfsfix -n checks
items.note: The Windows harness now captures an actual child-process termination during NTFS writes, then compares bounded raw $MFT/$BITMAP snapshots from the crash state to the post-chkdsk-repair state. ntfsfix -n remains secondary evidence only. This is a real Windows crash/checker lifecycle, but it is not yet a native MountFile replay fixture: full replay parity still requires a captured $LogFile transaction and byte-level comparison against native replay output.

Native NTFS operation chain (NtfsNativeWriter on a clean mkntfs volume) now has a declared 6-step injection matrix (copy, gate_pre, data_write, post_verify, identity_verify, publish) with the same per-cell contract: reach assertion, fail-closed propagation, byte-identical source, no surviving stage, plus a control cell; the application NTFS chain keeps its own declared matrix in tests/test_ntfs_write_phase_injection.py. JBD2 transaction sub-phases are instrumented via the checkpoint executor fault boundaries (PR #578).
